{"number":1707,"title":"A task declares what its run does to pull requests, and the executor resolves the target once","body":"Closes #1695

## The problem

Which pull request a task's run works on was decided in three places, none of them the task's declaration: the update worker disposed of its own incumbent, the generated-file lane reused an open PR by branch prefix, and an agent session picked its own branch with nothing telling it whether one already existed. A task could not say "append to my open PR" at all.

## What changes

**`expected_outcome` becomes four words** that carry the write ceiling and the target policy in one axis: `no_code_changes`, `fresh_pr`, `amend_existing_or_create_new_pr`, `supersede_existing_pr`. The retired `none`/`pr` normalize at the door beside `open-pr`/`merged-pr`, both declaration checks advise the rename, and the retirement rides #1642 with the contract's other tolerances.

**The executor resolves the target once** (`queue/target.mjs`), after the precondition's go and before code-work, and hands it to both phases: code-work as `CLAUDINITE_TARGET_MODE` / `CLAUDINITE_TARGET_BRANCH` / `CLAUDINITE_TARGET_PR`, the agent as `Target-branch:` / `Target-pr:` / `Supersedes:` fields stamped at the hand-off. A task's open pull requests are recognised by the branch prefix the executor mints (`claudinite/<pack>/<task>/`) or by the `Claudinite-Task:` trailer on the head commit. An amend reads the newest incumbent's mergeability and falls back to a fresh branch on a conflict or an unreadable answer. A supersede judges the newest incumbent by the runs on its head: a green, unlanded one on an auto-merge repo is landed and the occurrence ends there; otherwise the incumbents close once the run's own pull request exists, performed by the executor after code-work delivered one and by the session's converge (`--pr`) when the agent did. A run that delivers nothing leaves them where they were.

**The lanes take the target as given.** `deliverGenerated` accepts `branch`/`pr`; the update worker pushes to the branch it is handed. Each keeps its own discovery only under an executor that predates the hand-off, marked `@legacy-tolerance … retire:#1698`.

**What each canon task declares.** `none` tasks declare `no_code_changes`. `update` declares `supersede_existing_pr` (what its disposal already did, moved into the executor) and `usage-fold` `amend_existing_or_create_new_pr` (what its prefix reuse already did). By owner decision, nine more change behaviour: prose-to-checks-sweep, growth-extract, wiki-growth, improve-comments, ci-performance, growth-discover-packs and growth-promote amend their open pull request; rule-revalidation and growth-dedup supersede theirs. Their `task.md` files now deliver on the branch and pull request the item names instead of searching for a standing pull request or minting a branch themselves. Three consequences of one branch per run: wiki-growth's `no-open-pr-touching:product-wiki/` precondition retires (the amend is what that gate existed to prevent), a discovery run authors one pack per run rather than one per gap, and a promote run names a technology with no home on its tracker rather than minting the stub in a second pull request. Every other `pr` task declares `fresh_pr`, unchanged in behaviour.

Design: tasks-dispatch DESIGN §6 step 4b and decision §15.32; the sim models no pull request content, so the coverage map points at `queue/target.test.mjs` and the executor loop's tests.

## Verification

- Every new test was written red first: contract, declaration checks, work-item fields, converge ops, code-work env, the target planner and its I/O shell, the executor loop, the lanes, and the nine tasks' declarations and worker docs.
- Full suite over `git ls-files '*.test.mjs'`: 3265 tests, 0 failures.
- `check_the_work --changed --base origin/main`: no findings. `check_the_world`: 0 blocking; the one advisory on a touched file (`file-placement` on the update worker's import) is on a line this branch did not change.
- Production verification (a member's next `update` superseding its open PR; the canon's next `usage-fold` amending its own) is filed by `verify-in-production` after this merges, per basics.

A run that delivers nothing leaves them where they were.

**The lanes take the target as given.** `deliverGenerated` accepts `branch`/`pr`; the update worker pushes to the branch it is handed. Each keeps its own discovery only under an executor that predates the hand-off, marked `@legacy-tolerance … retire:#1698`.

**What each canon task declares.** `none` tasks declare `no_code_changes`. `update` declares `supersede_existing_pr` (what its disposal already did, moved into the executor) and `usage-fold` `amend_existing_or_create_new_pr` (what its prefix reuse already did). By owner decision, nine more change behaviour: prose-to-checks-sweep, growth-extract, wiki-growth, improve-comments, ci-performance, growth-discover-packs and growth-promote amend their open pull request; rule-revalidation and growth-dedup supersede theirs. Their `task.md` files now deliver on the branch and pull request the item names instead of searching for a standing pull request or minting a branch themselves. Three consequences of one branch per run: wiki-growth's `no-open-pr-touching:product-wiki/` precondition retires (the amend is what that gate existed to prevent), a discovery run authors one pack per run rather than one per gap, and a promote run names a technology with no home on its tracker rather than minting the stub in a second pull request. Every other `pr` task declares `fresh_pr`, unchanged in behaviour.

Design: tasks-dispatch DESIGN §6 step 4b and decision §15.32; the sim models no pull request content, so the coverage map points at `queue/target.test.mjs` and the executor loop's tests.

## Verification

- Every new test was written red first: contract, declaration checks, work-item fields, converge ops, code-work env, the target planner and its I/O shell, the executor loop, the lanes, and the nine tasks' declarations and worker docs.
- Full suite over `git ls-files '*.test.mjs'`: 3265 tests, 0 failures.
- `check_the_work --changed --base origin/main`: no findings. `check_the_world`: 0 blocking; the one advisory on a touched file (`file-placement` on the update worker's import) is on a line this branch did not change.
- Production verification (a member's next `update` superseding its open PR; the canon's next `usage-fold` amending its own) is filed by `verify-in-production` after this merges, per basics.

entries.name: mcp__github__actions_list
entries.description:
Tools for listing GitHub Actions resources.
Use this tool to list workflows in a repository, or list workflow runs, jobs, and artifacts for a specific workflow or workflow run.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (default: 30, max: 100)

resource_id.description:
The unique identifier of the resource. This will vary based on the "method" provided, so ensure you provide the correct ID:
- Do not provide any resource ID for 'list_workflows' method.
- Provide a workflow ID or workflow file name (e.g. ci.yaml) for 'list_workflow_runs' method, or omit to list all workflow runs in the repository.
- Provide a workflow run ID for 'list_workflow_jobs' and 'list_workflow_run_artifacts' methods.

filter.description: Filters jobs by their completed_at timestamp

workflow_jobs_filter.description: Filters for workflow jobs. **ONLY** used when method is 'list_workflow_jobs'

actor.description: Filter to a specific GitHub user's workflow runs.

branch.description: Filter workflow runs to a specific Git branch. Use the name of the branch.

event.description: Filter workflow runs to a specific event type

status.description: Filter workflow runs to only runs with a specific status

workflow_runs_filter.description: Filters for workflow runs. **ONLY** used when method is 'list_workflow_runs'

entries.name: mcp__github__get_job_logs
entries.description:
Get logs for GitHub Actions workflow jobs.
Use this tool to retrieve logs for a specific job or all failed jobs in a workflow run.
For single job logs, provide job_id. For all failed jobs in a run, provide run_id with failed_only=true.

failed_only.description: When true, gets logs for all failed jobs in the workflow run specified by run_id. Requires run_id to be provided.

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow job. Required when getting logs for a single job.

return_content.description: Returns actual log content instead of URLs

run_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run. Required when failed_only is true to get logs for all failed jobs in the run.

tail_lines.description: Number of lines to return from the end of the log

entries.name: mcp__github__list_commits
entries.description: Get list of commits of a branch in a GitHub repository. Returns at least 30 results per page by default, but can return more if specified using the perPage parameter (up to 100).

author.description: Author username or email address to filter commits by

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each commit. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields, e.g. just 'sha' and 'html_url'.

path.description: Only commits containing this file path will be returned

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

sha.description: Commit SHA, branch or tag name to list commits of. If not provided, uses the default branch of the repository. If a commit SHA is provided, will list commits up to that SHA.

since.description: Only commits after this date will be returned (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or YYYY-MM-DD)

until.description: Only commits before this date will be returned (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or YYYY-MM-DD)

entries.name: mcp__github__list_pull_requests
entries.description: List pull requests in a GitHub repository. If the user specifies an author, then DO NOT use this tool and use the search_pull_requests tool instead.

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each pull request. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'body' in particular drops the largest per-result data.

head.description: Filter by head user/org and branch

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

entries.name: mcp__github__pull_request_read
entries.description: Get information on a specific pull request in GitHub repository.

after.description: Cursor for pagination, used only by the get_review_comments method. Pass the endCursor from the previous page's PageInfo to fetch the next page.

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

entries.name: mcp__github__search_issues
entries.description: Search issues using natural-language semantic matching. Best for conceptual or paraphrased queries (e.g. "login fails after password reset"). Already scoped to is:issue.

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each issue result. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'body', 'reactions', and 'labels' in particular drops the largest per-result data.

owner.description: Optional repository owner. If provided with repo, only issues for this repository are listed.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

query.description: The search query, as natural language. When the user gives alternative wordings, include them as plain words rather than joining them with OR.

repo.description: Optional repository name. If provided with owner, only issues for this repository are listed.

sort.description: Sort field by number of matches of categories, defaults to best match

entries.name: mcp__github__list_issues
entries.description: List issues in a GitHub repository. For pagination, use the 'endCursor' from the previous response's 'pageInfo' in the 'after' parameter.

after.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the cursor from the previous response.

direction.description: Order direction. If provided, the 'orderBy' also needs to be provided.

field_name.description: Name of the custom field (e.g. "Priority"). Case-insensitive.

value.description: Value to filter on. For single-select fields, the option name (e.g. "P1"). For dates, YYYY-MM-DD. For numbers, the numeric value as a string. For text, the text value.

field_filters.description: Filter by custom issue field values. Each entry takes a field_name and a value; the server looks up the field and coerces the value to its type (single-select option name, text, number, or YYYY-MM-DD date).

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each issue. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'body' and 'field_values' in particular drops the largest per-result data.

orderBy.description: Order issues by field. If provided, the 'direction' also needs to be provided.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

state.description: Filter by state, by default both open and closed issues are returned when not provided

[{"sha":"33573d1c9028a696a8b5a2dd2356d3a47996b2f9","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/33573d1c9028a696a8b5a2dd2356d3a47996b2f9","message":"Promote 6 portable lessons from CrosswordChat, GCEC, LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite, Shepherd

Read the local packs of the six members named in #1861's Context
(CrosswordChat, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, hitbut, LaughCounter,
MissingBulbWebsite, Shepherd). hitbut and CrosswordChat's local packs carry
no portable candidates — hitbut's is an empty placeholder, and
CrosswordChat's is scoped entirely to its own host-page selectors and
calibrated timings.

Most candidates from the other four were already covered: the
GitHub-MCP-overflow (fields/per_page), git-checkout-onto-another-branch,
high-watermark-baseline-reanchoring, subscribe-every-open-PR,
list_pull_requests-merged-field, ToolSearch-fixed-roster, and several
subagent-dispatch rules were independently rediscovered but already live in
basics, git-github-advanced, or unattended-agents. A few referred to a
Claudinite mechanism already fixed since (converge-item.mjs's --repo/
--item-file), and one (a check's own explanatory comment self-matching) is
already solved generically by writing-repo-scanning-checks' stripComments
primitive (issue #201).

What's left is genuinely new and non-duplicate:

- git-github-advanced: list_pull_requests's head filter silently returns
  the wrong PR on a bare branch name (Shepherd, EdFringeNow's sibling
  finding independently); search_code's index can lag well behind a repo's
  real content for a fleet-wide sweep (Shepherd); the rendered PR-diff view
  can drop a new root-level file from its display (Shepherd); the spilled
  overflow file's shape is GitHub's {total_count, incomplete_results,
  items} envelope (Shepherd).
- claudinite-lifecycle: check_the_world.mjs and check_the_work.mjs cover
  disjoint rule scopes, so a green world run is not evidence the Stop hook
  will stay quiet (MissingBulbWebsite, #208's incident).
- claudinite-growth/unattended-agents: check whether an AskUserQuestion's
  answer is already decided (a loaded rule, a one-read-away state, the
  recommended option being the status quo) before firing it, and batch
  every open decision into one question (Shepherd, four measured sessions).

No pack version bumped and no VERSIONS.md row written — pack-version-bump's
job once this lands.

Growth-promote run over the members named in #1892's Context:
ClaudiniteCanary, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, Shepherd.

ClaudiniteCanary's local pack is deliberately trivial liveness probes
proving the canary repo's own realism as a Claudinite member — no rule
in it or its checks carries a portable opinion.

Shepherd's local pack turned up nothing new since it was last read for
PR #1886 (this same branch): the two RULES.md commits since then are a
revalidation already covered by the existing "stale diff base" rule in
git-github-advanced, and a deletion. Everything else in the file was
either already promoted in this PR's first commit, already live
elsewhere in the corpus, or stayed local (repo-specific timing/mechanism
detail, or now-stale complaints about a Claudinite script that has since
gained the --repo/--item-file flags it was missing).

GCEC had two genuinely new, non-duplicate lessons:

- **git-github-advanced**: `get_job_logs` can hit its own token cap the
  same way a guessed-too-large `tail_lines` does — sharpened the existing
  "read get_job_logs with a generous tail_lines" line, which was in fact
  wrong advice on its own terms.
- **claudinite-growth/unattended-agents**: a duplicate dispatch trigger
  while your own delegated subagent still owns an item is normally the
  echo of your own claim, not a competing session — resolve it via the
  dispatch's own check and stop, rather than letting "just confirming"
  escalate into independently redoing (and duplicating) the subagent's
  work.

Everything else read from GCEC (the GitHub-MCP-overflow rules, the
architecture/extractor-pipeline rules, the ambiguous-date and
prefer-JSON-LD rules, the high-watermark-baseline pattern, the
scratchpad-can't-import-project-deps rule) was either GCEC product-
specific or already live in `basics`, `node`, `html`, `web-scraping`, or
`basics/skills/writing-tests`. One check-scope gap GCEC's RULES.md still
describes (`gha/scheduled-failure-escalation` seeing only `schedule:`
triggers) is no longer true of the check as declared — skipped as stale,
not promoted.

`pack-version-bump`'s job once this lands.

Growth-promote run over the members named in #1938's Context:
ClaudiniteWebsite, EdFringeNow.

Read both members' local packs (RULES.md and their check modules),
generalized the candidates, and deduped against the whole corpus.

Most candidates were already covered: ClaudiniteWebsite's node --test
discovery check duplicates the canon node-test-discovery skill; its
site-version-tooltip check is a project-specific instance of the
sharedConstants drift-guard rule already in basics; several of its
subagent/checkout-safety and "vendor-set gap vs canon gap" rules are
already live in unattended-agents and claudinite-lifecycle almost
verbatim; and its canon-patch-via-issue and stale converge-item.mjs
workarounds are Claudinite's-own-shape specifics that don't generalize.
EdFringeNow's RULES.md has clearly already been mined heavily in prior
rounds — its UTC-crossing-at-the-edge, cache-generation-fingerprint,
unknown-is-a-state, browser-evidence-before-repro, and instruction-
poisoning-guard lessons are already live in web-scraping, static-website,
basics and claudinite-growth/extracting-lessons almost word for word,
and its headless-browser font/pinning/capture traps already match
headless-browser's RULES.md near-verbatim.

What's left is genuinely new and non-duplicate:

- **spec-driven-product**: reserve the `feature` comment class for a
  product-behavior change — a repo-tooling or process change has no
  requirement leaf to record, so mislabeling it `feature` arms
  doc-first-red-by-default against a target that can't exist; don't
  launder a mislabeling with a backdated spec commit or a coverage
  allowlist entry (EdFringeNow, from its own incident and recovery).
- **claudinite-tasks**: a queue item's own delivered PR must never carry
  a closing keyword for that item's issue — GitHub's auto-close on merge
  races ahead of `converge-item.mjs`'s comment-and-label transition and
  can override an intended `needs-human-approval` park. Already a settled
  rule in Claudinite's own local pack (#49) and independently rediscovered
  by ClaudiniteWebsite, but never promoted to the shared `queue/
  instructions.md` every member actually reads.
- **headless-browser**: a sandboxed agent's egress proxy can deny a
  headless browser's own connection to a host that `curl`/`WebFetch`
  reaches fine (no shared tunnel path) — fetch the real asset once with
  a working tool and serve it from disk via route interception rather
  than concluding the host is unreachable (EdFringeNow, unpkg.com).

`pack-version-bump`'s job once this lands.

{"number":1794,"title":"Verify in production: a drain says the unreadable hold once, not per item","body":"Original-issue: #1791
In-production-when: a `claudinite-executor.yml` run on this repository, on a head sha at or after `8c1dd40`, has completed having drained TWO OR MORE items — its job log ends with two or more `- #<n>: <outcome>` lines
Verify: in that same job log, the line `CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL is not readable live by this run's token` appears AT MOST ONCE, and the retired wording `could not read CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL live` does not appear at all
Not-before: 2026-09-07T09:00:00.000Z
Retry-every: 1 day
Model: sonnet

The unit tests pin the reader itself: an access refusal is asked once, said once, and never asked
again; a 5xx keeps asking but still prints once. What they cannot reach is the WIRING — that
`executor.mjs` builds one `liveSuspendReader` for the drain instead of a fresh one per boundary. A
per-boundary construction would pass every test in `suspend.test.mjs` and reproduce the exact
symptom this change fixes, and only a real multi-item drain shows the difference.

## For the run

1. Read `In-production-when:` against this repo's actual executor runs — `actions_list` for
   `claudinite-executor.yml`, then the job log of the newest completed run at or after `8c1dd40`.
   A run that drained one item or none does not answer; that is "not yet live".
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the run URL, the number of items drained and the
   count of the line, and close this issue completed. Fails: reopen #1791 with the run URL, how
   many times the line appeared and how many items were drained; comment here linking that; close
   this issue completed, because the verification did its job by finding the fault.
3. **Not yet live** → set `Not-before:` to now + 1 day (the instant you are reading at, not the old
   value), clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, leave it open. No comment.

Converge with `converge-item.mjs` and make the calls it prints; never write a `task:status:*` label
by hand.

{"number":1774,"title":"Per-pack task tests assert the pack's own code, not the task mechanism","body":"Blocked-by: #1755
Automerge: test-changes

<!-- filed by /do-later -->

Owner ruling: a test belongs to the code it exercises. A pack's test of one of its tasks proves that pack's own code — its task-local `preconditions.mjs` terms, its workers, its declared merge-rules classes, and any genuinely intricate use of the mechanism (a composed `||` expression the pack designed, a `schedule_after` chain, a fan-out) — never that the task mechanism runs a plain declaration: nothing is learned from asserting that `due:weekly` parses as a weekly cadence, that a built-in term declares the signal it reads, or that a declaration validates. The mechanism's own suite (`packs/claudinite-tasks/test/`) proves the mechanism once, for every declaration.

## The sweep

Read every `packs/*/test/` test whose subject is a task declaration — today `chrome-extension/test/tasks.test.mjs`, `claudinite-canon-curation/test/tasks.test.mjs`, `claudinite-growth/test/tasks.test.mjs`, `claudinite-lifecycle/test/tasks.test.mjs`, and any sibling in `basics`, `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog`, `product-wiki`, `tidy-repo`, `claudinite-dashboard` whose name or body names a task — and in each:

- **Delete** assertions that re-run the mechanism over the declaration: `taskCadence(decl)` equalling the term the file states; `preconditionSignals(...)` equalling the built-ins' signal list; `validateTaskDeclaration(decl)` being empty (the `task-declaration-shape` check judges every declaration over the real tree already); `evaluatePrecondition` driven only to show a built-in run-history or movement term holds or declines; and every self-pin of a declared literal (`agent_model`, `expected_outcome`, `automerge`, `invocation_endpoint`, `code_work_timeout` equalling what the file says).
- **Keep, and where thin, strengthen** what proves the pack's own code: a task-local term's decisions over fabricated signals (which members a fleet term selects, that an unproven fleet state errors rather than reading as nothing), a worker's behaviour, a merge-rules class's verdicts over file lists, and a two-artifact claim that could drift (a worker file the declaration names exists; a workflow runs the worker the declaration names).
- **Keep** a mechanism assertion only where the usage is intricate — the composition is the pack's design, not the term's — and say so in the test's comment in one line.
- A test file left with nothing of the pack's own to prove is deleted whole; a pack-level roster test ("the pack keeps exactly these tasks") stays only where it pins a two-artifact claim (a catalog row, a README table) and not the directory listing to itself.

`packs/claudinite-tasks/test/` is the mechanism's own suite and is out of scope: there, the mechanism is the code under test.

## Write the rule down

Add one bullet to `packs/basics/skills/writing-tests/SKILL.md`, beside the "Never pin a declaration to itself" bullet, stating the ruling above in the skill's own register: a test proves the code it belongs to, not the mechanism it uses; a mechanism assertion in a consumer's test earns its place only for intricate usage, named in the test. One sentence, near forty words, no restatement of the sweep.

## Done when

- Every kept assertion in the swept files reads as a claim about that pack's own code or an intricate usage named as such.
- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` is green with the suite's test count lower, not higher; `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs --changed --base origin/main` and `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` report no blocking finding.
- The PR body lists, per pack, how many tests were removed and which were kept as intricate usage.

Owner ruling: `Automerge: test-changes` — a diff of test files alone lands itself; the skill bullet in the same diff parks the PR for the owner's review, which is the intended gate for a rule.

input.title: Should a later amend run's park end the earlier run's park on the same pull request?
input.body:
**Waiting on the owner's decision.** Nothing here is queued work until somebody picks an option. Filed by the production retrospective on #1695 / #1707, running as #1718.

## What the record shows

`amend_existing_or_create_new_pr` works exactly as designed. Over the week after #1707 merged (2026-09-05T11:00Z → 2026-09-12T19:38Z) the executor resolved a target for 68 items across 20 `claudinite-executor.yml` runs — 22 `this task changes no code`, 43 fresh, 3 amend, **zero** fresh-branch fallbacks and **zero** unresolvable targets. The one task whose pull request stayed open amended it rather than opening a second:

| run | item | resolution | effect on #1886 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-07 10:45 | #1861 | fresh | opened it |
| 2026-09-08 20:14 | #1892 | `amending #1886, which has no conflicts with its base` | 2nd commit |
| 2026-09-11 09:59 | #1928 | `amending #1886, which has no conflicts with its base` | none — the run found nothing to promote |
| 2026-09-12 09:34 | #1938 | `amending #1886, which has no conflicts with its base` | 3rd commit |

#1886 carries exactly three commits, one per run that had something to say. Four separate open pull requests (#1303, #1419, #1690, #1715, all closed by hand on 2026-09-06) became one. That is what the change was for, and it is working.

## The cost the design did not address

Each of those runs is its own work item, and each one that delivers parks `task:status:needs-human-approval` naming the same pull request. #1861, #1892 and #1938 are all open right now, all saying "merge or close #1886". The count rises by one per delivering run for as long as #1886 is unreviewed.

Nothing collapses them. `SUPERSEDABLE_PARKS` (`packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/janitor-rules.mjs:40`) is `['failure', 'action']` by the deliberate decision recorded at `janitor-rules.mjs:140` — an approval park is never superseded by a later clean run. They do end together: rule G's `Ends-when: #1886 closed` closes all three when the pull request resolves, so this is bounded and self-clearing, not a leak.

This is the retrospective brief's stated overuse signal firing ("the approval-park count for that task rises while no pull request of it merges"): three open parks, zero growth-promote pull requests merged in the window. It is **not** evidence that amend is the wrong choice here — the prior state was strictly worse. The question is narrower than the signal's suggested remedy.

## The question

When an amend run pushes onto the pull request an earlier run's park already names, is the earlier park answered?

- **A — leave it.** Three parks, one pull request, all ending together. Costs one open issue per day of review latency. No code changes.
- **B — a later amend item's park ends the earlier item's park of the same task naming the same `Target-pr:`.** The later park names the same pull request and its body now carries the later work, so the earlier question genuinely is answered. Strictly narrower than adding `approval` to `SUPERSEDABLE_PARKS`, which would be wrong for exactly the reasons `janitor-rules.mjs:140` records.
- **C — `growth-promote` declares `supersede_existing_pr` instead.** One pull request per run again, which is what #1707 moved away from.
- **D — a narrower `automerge` policy for `growth-promote`**, so its rounds land instead of queueing for review.

**B** is the recommendation: it is the smallest change that matches what actually happened, and it leaves the amend/supersede choice per task where the design put it.

input.title: Two module headers cite `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` twice in one parenthesis
input.body:
A doubled citation, left by the sweep that re-pointed the deleted design docs' `§`-numbered references at the packs that absorbed them (#1887):

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/target.mjs:1-2` — `(docs/PRINCIPLES.md,\n// docs/PRINCIPLES.md)`
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs:29-30` — `(PRINCIPLES.md,\n// PRINCIPLES.md)`

Each was a two-pointer citation (`§6 step 4b and decision §15.32`, and its sibling) whose two halves both resolved to the same surviving document. Both sites read as a typo now.

The fix is to drop the duplicate half in each, leaving one pointer. Nothing depends on it; this is a comment correction, not behaviour.

Worth noting because it is the failure mode the local pack's own rule names — *"Verifying a sweep that rewrote citations — read every rewritten site … a doubled citation or one repointed at an unrelated live doc carries no old token"* — and neither site carries a grep-able old token, so nothing else will surface them. The doubling also spans a line break, which is why a single-line grep for it comes back empty.

Found by the production retrospective on #1695 / #1707 while reading `target.mjs`; that run fixes nothing itself.
